extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, graduate students, and educators writing mathematical notes and exposition
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for producing rigorous, example-rich, visually integrated mathematics lecture notes and expository writing; emphasizes precision in definitions, building examples, teaching-as-learning, TeX typesetting skills, and making geometric intuition visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor as virtue (annoying precision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics should be 'annoyingly' precise: do not skip careful definitions or hand-wave; skipping careful definition is a sign of muddled thinking, not sophistication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer being tedious about a definition to waving hands. Adopt an ethos of relentless attention to detail; the blog title itself endorses this stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a large stock of examples (examples first)
rubrics_metrics.description: A good stock of examples, as large as possible, is indispensable for a thorough understanding of any concept; when learning something new, first build examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize constructing and collecting examples over polishing theorem statements; an extensive example library is often more valuable than a polished abstract formulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach to learn / write as pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing notes and exposition functions as a pedagogical exercise: 'the best way to learn is to teach.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose notes with the mindset of teaching others — this clarifies understanding and exposes gaps. Use note-writing as an active learning tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live-TeX lectures and technical typesetting practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Use live-TeX lectures as a 'good exercise' for developing technical skills, particularly for typesetting nontrivial objects like commutative diagrams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ TeX in lecture-note workflows to practice reproducible, high-quality typesetting; use live typesetting to hone presentation of technical material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual integration / make the visualisable visible
rubrics_metrics.description: For geometry-heavy or intuition-driven material, integrate hand-drawn illustrations and visual depictions so that curves on surfaces and geometric features are shown rather than merely described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use drawing tools (e.g., tablet apps like Paper) to produce diagrams that concretize abstract notions. Bridge abstract mathematics with geometric intuition by making visuals explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaim limitations and be humble about completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge limitations of one's notes: state that they may not be complete or correct while still being potentially useful to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include humble disclaimers about completeness/correctness to set reader expectations; recognize usefulness of imperfect notes rather than glossing over gaps.
